native_result.query: What is the proportion of junior professors in replicated studies in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: In Psychology, replicated studies have a much higher proportion of junior professor (64.7%) and in the original studies the senior professors are more represented (82.4%)
native_result.HypoB: In psychological replication studies (specifically within the Reproducibility Project: Psychology, RPP), the proportion of junior professors (Assistant Professors) among successfully replicated studies is approximately 28.57% (10 out of 35) across the complete sample, or 32.26% (10 out of 31) when excluding flagged studies (drop == False). Among all attempted psychology replications in RPP, junior professors lead 23.71% (23/97) to 24.44% (22/90) of the replication teams, whereas original psychology studies contain 0% junior professors. The seniority of replication leads (junior professors vs senior professors/researchers) does not significantly impact replication success (p = 0.46).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Loaded meta-regression study dataset. 2. Filtered for Psychology discipline and RPP project. 3. Calculated exact proportions of Assistant Professors for replicated studies (both all and drop==False) and overall replication studies. 4. Evaluated original study author seniority baseline (0% junior professors). 5. Performed 2x2 Fisher exact and chi-square independence tests.
